Barry Sternlicht founded Starwood buying subprime apartment buildings, and turning them into hotels.

comments.author: @HowDealsWork
comments.text: The quiet logic behind all those brands is that most big hotel companies don't own the buildings. They sell a flag, a booking system and a loyalty programme to owners and earn fees. So when two chains merge, the buyer isn't really paying for real estate. It's paying for fee streams and loyalty members, and each extra brand is another way to sign an owner who would otherwise compete with an existing flag down the street.

comments.text:
Of their brands I found the Hilton Garden inn and Citizen M great value. The room size of the HGI in Downtown Manhattan was excellent for NYC, much better than Double Tree Downtown. The room meant connectivity at Citizen M meant I could connect my streaming apps off my phone straight to the tv in seconds and turn the lights off from the iPad lay in bed, virtually no other hotel offer this. I used CM in DC and LA.I did enjoy the Hyatt Centric Midtown before the price shot up. 
Another Hotel Brand offering a very wide variety of quality is Best Western 

I live in the U.K. and Double Tree is my go to Hilton brand and Novotel my go to Accor Brand though Ibis is great value in Eastern Europe.  

What is missing in the U.S. is Premier Inn, they are the nicest budget brand by far and have a near universal standard bar a few older properties. A lot of the budget brands in the U.S. have very poor standards not helped by the types of people frequenting them e.g. Days Inn.
